note: Primitive state-forest campground and day-use area on the south shore of Hungry Man Lake, about 10 miles south of Itasca State Park: sites on a pine-covered rise above the lake, with a drive-in boat ramp and a swimming area. Managed by Itasca State Park. --Claude
summary: DNR record + forest guide read: 14 primitive sites on a pine-covered rise above the lake, vault toilet, drinking water, boat ramp; $17 tax-included confirmed; first come, first served. Lakeview could not be confirmed (sites invisible under continuous pine canopy, no site photos read): downgrade to not waterfront flagged. Phone differs from the DNR's manager number.
flags: WATERFRONT (checked hard): downgrade lakeview -> not waterfront (unsure after every source read). The DNR says only 'The campsites sit on a pine covered rise above Hungry Man Lake.' Imagery shows the campground ridge (Google/DNR points 47.0603,-95.1829 / 47.060578,-95.182609) under continuous pine canopy with no pad, loop or vehicle visible; the ridge's north tip reaches the shore about 110 m north of those points, and an open marshy meadow lies on each side. The stored evidence ('sites set back behind a shore road/day-use strip, near-shore sites overlook the lake', satellite at 47.0598,-95.1840) could not be reproduced: that point is the brushy meadow west of the ridge with only the access road through it. No site numbers, site map or site photos exist on the DNR pages; Google photos/reviews were not read and could support lakeview if they show the lake from a site.
